en.name: Saints Simon and Jude, Apostles
en.summary: Joint feast of two lesser-documented apostles, Simon the Zealot and Jude Thaddaeus, patron of desperate and hopeless causes.
en.body: This joint feast honors two of the Twelve Apostles about whom Scripture records comparatively little beyond their names in the apostolic lists. Simon is distinguished by the title "the Zealot," suggesting possible earlier association with the Jewish nationalist movement resisting Roman occupation, though the term's exact meaning in his case remains debated by scholars. Jude, also called Thaddaeus and traditionally distinguished from Judas Iscariot, asks Jesus a question at the Last Supper recorded in John's Gospel and is traditionally credited with authorship of the brief New Testament Epistle of Jude. Strong tradition holds the two carried out missionary work together in Persia, where both were martyred, and Jude in particular became one of the most popularly invoked saints in Catholic devotion, venerated as the patron of desperate and seemingly hopeless causes.
